analysis.title: Rates Spark: Treasury heat from tech flight - but for how long?
key_insights: The US 10yr yield is down about 50bp from its recent highs. Drivers are real money value buyers, fast money longs in Treasuries versus payers in SOFR (a short swap spread trade), and a risk-off tone in AI stocks that has pushed money into Treasuries.
The AI risk-off tone has driven the last 10-15bp of the decline, taking the 10yr yield to the low 4.80s%. If the AI selloff intensifies, long-end yields would likely fall further.
ING sees the 4.65% area for the 10yr yield as a possible settling level if risk-off intensifies. The technical picture for AI valuations does not look good for the next few weeks.
A slow drift lower in equities would eventually be ignored by Treasuries, but a large equity drop would not. ING is not calling for a large drop but is watching for it.
The market has ignored elevated inflation, large fiscal deficits and the ongoing AI growth boost. ING expects Treasuries to refocus on fundamentals at some point.
The VIX jumped to its highest since March on Thursday as tech stocks came under pressure.
The 10y OAT/Bund spread ended a brief recovery below 150bp and widened again, on risk-off sentiment and protest headlines in France that highlight the difficulty of consolidating French finances.

The Bank of England hiked as expected, and every committee member voted to hike. Revised inflation forecasts add upside risk to rates, and markets price a 50% chance of the next hike in December plus at least one more in 2027.

Sterling rates up to 2Y rose after the BoE, but the 10Y swap rate ended lower. ING reads this as markets front-loading hikes while doubting the BoE's terminal rate, and ING also doubts the BoE ends hiking near 4.5%.
ING thinks the sterling curve is too steep compared with euro and dollar curves.

US jobs data is due Friday. Consensus is +65k October payrolls (September 29k) and unemployment at 4.2%. ING says only a large surprise would shift focus from AI concerns, given the low-hire / low-fire pattern.

risk_factors: A large equity selloff would push Treasury yields down sharply.
Upside inflation surprises or another jump in oil or gas prices could make BoE pricing more hawkish.
Protests in France could pressure French spreads further.
Treasuries could refocus on elevated inflation and large fiscal deficits.
vol_and_positioning: The VIX rose to its highest level since March on Thursday as tech stocks sold off.
Fast money holds long Treasury positions versus paying fixed in SOFR swaps, a short swap spread trade.
Real money buyers, mostly domestic with some international, have bought Treasuries at higher yields.
geopolitical: Protests in France highlight the political challenge of consolidating public finances.
US election result: ING says electorate support for fewer data centres and more scrutiny of AI may be a factor in the AI selloff, though broader valuation pressure matters more.

tension_points.bull_case: Real money value buying, fast money longs and safety flows from the AI selloff have pushed the 10yr yield down about 50bp, and further equity losses would push it lower.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation is elevated, fiscal deficits are large, the AI growth boost continues and unemployment is low at 4.2%, so Treasuries could refocus on fundamentals.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A large equity dump would extend the yield fall. A creeping equity decline would eventually be ignored by Treasuries.
